review: The Arabic splits the opener over two lines (حَدِيثَ الْـ / ـفَادِي) as a typesetting artefact of a long word. Hebrew does not split words across lines, so each stanza opens with a short line and puts the epithet on the next.
Stanza 4 lines 6–8 repeat 1:2–1:4 verbatim, as in the Arabic; only the opening line differs (فَذَاكَ خَيْرُ حَدِيثٍ / 'for that is the best tale').
1:8 וְאֵין מָקוֹם לְהִוָּלֵד — 'and no place to be born', for وَلَا مَكَانٌ لِيُولَد; the infinitive is passive in sense, matching the Arabic.
3:6 לְכָל־עָנִי וְחוֹלֶה — 'to every poor and sick one', for بِكُلِّ عَانٍ سَقِيم; the Arabic's two adjectives are turned into two nouns, which is how Hebrew pairs them.
4:4 הַבְּנִיּוּת — 'adoption/sonship', for التَّبَنِّي; the noun is post-biblical but is the fixed theological term and appears in the Hebrew NT for υἱοθεσία.
